messages:
IncidentBot: Paging on-call: P99 streaming tail latency > 5s across eu-west2 -> observed spike at 2026-03-15T10:12:39Z :rotating_light:
Ana (oncall): ack — looking. Any customer-facing alerts?
Kate (support): we have ~12 customers reporting degraded streaming sessions (timeouts, partial responses). Raising CS ticket numbers: CS-8942.
Ana (oncall): grabbing dashboards — p95 up ~600ms, p99 jumped to 5.2s for streaming endpoints in eu-west2, also increased RTOs on websocket handshakes.
Ryan (neteng): seeing increased SYN retransmits from nodes in eu-west2 -> NAT egress path; some flows are staying in FIN_WAIT. Could be ephemeral port reuse / conntrack saturation.
Priya (sre): any DNS spikes? our streaming clients do some name churn on boot.
Ryan (neteng): DNS query failures spiked concurrently for external DNS (8.8.8.8) at ~10:10Z, delayed responses causing TLS handshake timeouts. Trace: many flows hitting the NAT gateway and returning RSTs.
Ana (oncall): running quick checks — `kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=nat-gw -o wide` shows 1/3 nat-gw replicas Ready (others CrashLoopBackoff).
Priya (sre): omg, that explains it. If nat-gw pool scaled down/disrupted, ephemeral port exhaustion can cause heavy tail latency for new TCP/TLS sessions.
Ana (oncall): I'm promoting a page to SEV-2 — bringing in neteng and infra. @Ryan can you confirm nat-gw health and logs?
Ryan (neteng): logs indicate `nf_conntrack` buffer saturation on the host: kernel messages: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" around 10:09Z. Also notable DNS response timeouts from our egress path.
Priya (sre): mitigation plan: 1) scale nat-gw to restore capacity, 2) bump conntrack limits on affected hosts temporarily, 3) reroute egress via secondary NAT cluster, 4) inform customers of mitigation and expected recovery.
Ana (oncall): executing 1 & 2 now. Running: `kubectl -n infra scale deploy nat-gw --replicas=4` and `for node in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do kubectl debug $node -- chroot /host sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000; done` (will run via deploy job for safety).
DeployBot: Deployment nat-gw scaled to 4 replicas (triggered by Ana).
Kate (support): posting interim note to affected customers: "We’re investigating streaming disruptions in eu-west2. Engineers are performing mitigations; next update in 15 minutes."
Priya (sre): added temp iptables rule to drop long-idle tracked flows: `conntrack -L | awk '$8 > 300 {print $0}'` then `conntrack -D -s <ip>` — targeted until conntrack freed. Doing this on 3 nodes.
Ryan (neteng): started failover of egress via nat-cluster-b (secondary) by flipping BGP route for affected subnets; propagation should be ~30s-90s.
Ana (oncall): p95 is already improving to ~220ms in eu-west2; p99 trending down to ~1.1s. Streaming stalls still visible but fewer.
Priya (sre): careful — we briefly saw some streaming reconnect storms when nat-gw restored; throttled control plane to avoid cascading restarts (`kubectl rollout pause`).
Kate (support): customers reporting some sessions recovered; updating CS-8942 that mitigations are in progress and we expect full recovery in 10-20m.
Ana (oncall): observed TLS handshake failures drop by ~80% after reroute. Collecting packet captures and `ss -s` summaries for postmortem.
Ryan (neteng): capturing `iptables -L -v -n` and `conntrack -S` outputs, saving to S3 at s3://redwood-incident-captures/2956799999/ for analysis.
Priya (sre): temporary measures applied: conntrack_max bumped, nat-gw replicas to 4, egress reroute to nat-cluster-b, conntrack pruning. Need root cause: why nat-gw replicas lost readiness.
Ana (oncall): Check logs for nat-gw containers: `kubectl -n infra logs deployment/nat-gw --since=20m` — I see OOMKilled on 2 pods around 10:05Z. Memory pressure could be due to `conntrack` table growth interacting with agent memory use.
Priya (sre): opening a ticket to infra-team: INFRA-2079 — investigate nat-gw OOM and add resource limits + liveness tweaks.
Ryan (neteng): possible contributing factor: upstream DNS provider rate-limited responses leading to client-level retries; high retry rate increases ephemeral port churn. Suggest adding DNS caching or enabling keepalive for our streaming clients.
Kate (support): customers asking about SLA impact — what's the current SLO breach window?
Ana (oncall): preliminary numbers: 10:08Z-10:23Z p99 > SLO threshold (5s) for streaming create/connect calls. Estimated affected requests ~42k, impacted customers ~12 (tier mix: 9 standard, 3 enterprise). I'll generate exact query later.
Priya (sre): collecting slow request traces: `SELECT * FROM traces WHERE service='streaming' AND duration>2000ms AND timestamp>'2026-03-15T10:00:00Z'` — storing in incident archive.
Ana (oncall): I'll hand off to Priya for next shift. Handoff summary: nat-gw OOM -> conntrack table saturation -> TLS/DNS timeouts -> streaming tail latency and p99 SLO breach. Mitigations applied: scaled nat-gw, bumped conntrack_max, pruned conntrack, rerouted egress, applying DNS caching recommendation. Customer impact: ~42k requests affected, major reduction after mitigations, monitoring for regression.
Priya (sre): taking over. Next actions: 1) full postmortem with root cause (OOM vs conntrack behaviour), 2) schedule permanent conntrack increase + graceful pruning, 3) add horizontal autoscaler for nat-gw and readiness probe improvements, 4) short-term recommendation to client teams to enable client-side DNS caching or keepalives.
Ryan (neteng): I'll follow up on DNS provider logs and BGP route metrics. Also recommend adding synthetic egress probes to detect NAT saturation earlier.
Kate (support): I'll draft a customer incident summary for the affected customers and coordinate any SLA credits once postmortem is complete.
IncidentBot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 2026-03-15T10:45:50Z — latencies returned to within SLO for p95 and p99 trending below thresholds. :white_check_mark:
Ana (oncall): thanks team — handoff complete. Priya, assigning follow-ups to INFRA-2079 and NET-1985.
Priya (sre): acknowledged. Adding links to runbook snippets used: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/net/nat-ephemeral-handling and capture bundle s3://redwood-incident-captures/2956799999/
Kate (support): final note to customers sent: "Issue mitigated; full postmortem and timeline will be shared once complete." :wave:
